Jamal K.: Quick q — planning to start parental leave May 1. Can I stack accrued vacation so I can be off until June 1?
Michelle (People Ops): Yep, you can apply PTO on top of company-paid parental leave. There are a couple of operational bits (payroll coding, benefits proration). Looping in Sara from benefits. :wave:
Sara (Benefits): Hi! You can stack PTO. Two things to decide: 1) do you want PTO applied as leave (counts as continuous service) or paid out, and 2) are you planning a temporary FTE change when you return? Both affect premiums and HSA contributions.
Jamal K.: I want PTO applied (not cashed out) so service remains continuous. Also thinking of 4 weeks at 80% FTE after I return to ramp back — will that affect health coverage?
Lena - Eng Mgr: From scheduling side, 80% for a month is fine. Ill update on-call and coordinate coverage. Please tell Eng staffing when you submit. :+1:
Sara (Benefits): Short-term 80% typically keeps active coverage. Premiums/proration happen at payroll; employer HSA contributions may be prorated for partial-pay periods. Wel need exact dates to calculate costs.
Jamal K.: Do I need a special form to attach PTO to parental leave, or just the parental leave request with a note?
Michelle (People Ops): Submit the Parental Leave request in the HR portal and add a comment "PTO applied" and attach a PTO transfer screenshot if you like. Wel flag the record so Payroll codes it as paid parental + PTO. If you want the 80% ramp, sign the temporary FTE amendment (we have a template).
Payroll Bot: Automated reminder: submit leave+PTO combos before payroll cutoff for correct gross/pay coding. HR link: https://hr.redwood.example/leave-forms
Jamal K.: One more — equity vesting? If I use PTO for the top-up weeks vs any unpaid time, does vesting continue?
Emma (Comp & Equity): Good q. PTO-applied weeks count as continuous service and do not pause vesting. Unpaid leave beyond company-paid parental time pauses vesting. Temporary FTE reductions do NOT pause vesting. Il update the vesting calendar when you confirm dates.
Jamal K.: Thanks. I'll submit today: 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-01 (company-paid first 6 weeks, then 2 weeks PTO applied). Il also upload the temporary FTE amendment for the 80% ramp starting 2026-06-02 for four weeks.
Michelle (People Ops): Perfect ll watch for your submission. Include "PTO applied" and attach the amendment. Il route to Payroll & Benefits and queue manager signature. Congrats in advance! :tada:
Lena - Eng Mgr: Il approve the FTE amendment once its in and coordinate the on-call rota and handoffs.
Jamal K.: Appreciate the help everyone. DMing Michelle the docs now. :pray:
